# nonObject

<link-summary>Checks whether a value is **not** an object.</link-summary>

<web-summary>nonObject() — Checks whether a value is **not** an object. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/base</code> · Since: 1.11.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function nonObject<T>(value: T | object): value is T;
```

`nonObject(value)` is the same test as `!isObject(value)`, written so that a guard clause reads as a sentence rather than as a negation.

The test is `typeof value === "object"` with `null` excluded, so arrays, dates and class instances all count, while a function does not. `isObjectLike` is the one that also accepts functions.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type          | Description         |
| :-------- | :------------ | :------------------ |
| `value`   | `T \| object` | The value to check. |

## Returns

`boolean` — `true` when the value is not an object; otherwise `false`.

In TypeScript the guard narrows `value` to `T` inside the branch.

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
nonObject(null); // => true
nonObject("abc"); // => true
nonObject(function () {}); // => true
nonObject({}); // => false
nonObject([]); // => false
nonObject(new Date()); // => false
```
